thread:
Sara (Support): hey team — AcmeInc seeing a wave of 429s from their private gateway after a traffic spike this morning. They say it's their customer-managed k8s ingress hitting a limit + our gateway returning 429s. Copied logs below and asking for config guidance.

AcmeInc - ops: yeah, we saw a big job fanout and then ~60% of requests got 429s for ~90s. Logs show upstream reset and rate-limiter exceed. We run nginx-ingress + envoy sidecar -> our gateway (onprem) -> redwood private. Not sure which throttle to raise.

Matt (Eng-SRE): quick checklist: is the ingress controller rate-limiting (nginx) or kube-proxy? Also check Envoy local rate limit filter and any iptables-based qdisc. Can you paste the 429 response headers?

AcmeInc - ops: headers snippet: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rate-limit: gateway:global:burst=100:limit=500/s
x-rw-instance: gw-02
x-rw-request-id: 01H9XJ2W2X
```

Maria (Support): note the x-rw header shows gateway-side global limit. That suggests the request reached the gateway and then got rate-limited there (not ingress). But ingress could be queuing and then causing bursts that trip gateway.

Jules (Eng-Runtime): two vectors: 1) upstream gateway global token bucket +/- burst, 2) per-connection/socket limits on Envoy or nginx causing resets that make the gateway see sudden simultaneous connections. For onprem we recommend: a) configure ingress-controller to smooth bursts (connection coalescing, keepalive) b) bump gateway burst and add local backoff policy c) enable prefix KV caching and request coalescing on client side if possible.

Aaditya (Eng-Platform): sharing typical k8s nginx-ingress tuning we use in private deployments that help with bursty clients:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: nginx-configuration
data:
  proxy-buffer-size: "16k"
  proxy-buffering: "on"
  keepalive-requests: "100"
  keepalive-timeout: "30"
  worker-connections: "8192"
  limit-connections: "0"
  limit-rpm: "0"
```
Also use `max-conns` on the service loadbalancer and `http2` config tuning if clients multiplex.

Matt (Eng-SRE): also check kube-proxy conntrack settings (net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max) — low conntrack can drop connections and lead to rapid retries.

AcmeInc - ops: we saw these in our envoy logs: 
```
[2026-02-18T11:02:14Z] envoy rate_limiter: local limit reached, rejecting request
[2026-02-18T11:02:15Z] upstream reset, remote_close
[2026-02-18T11:02:16Z] connection terminated: ECONNRESET
```

Jules (Eng-Runtime): what version of our onprem gateway are you on? older builds had a conservative default burst (100) that trips on short spikes. If you're on <1.8.0 we suggest bumping the gateway env var RW_GATEWAY_RATE_BURST or editing the config map entry `rate_limit.burst` for the instance to something like 500 for high-throughput customers.

AcmeInc - ops: running 1.7.2 — ok we can test bumping. Any guidance on safe values? We don't want to open up to DoS.

Maria (Support): balance is key. Recommend: step 1) add a short scaled test (2x traffic) with observability on token usage; step 2) add conservative gradual increase (100 -> 250 -> 500) with Canary window 5m; step 3) ensure per-tenant quotas remain enforced.

Aaditya (Eng-Platform): also enable the gateway autopolicy that falls back to a cheaper model when capacity tight. In config: 
```
rate_limit:
  enabled: true
  global_limit: "500/s"
  per_client: "200/s"
  burst: 300
  backoff_policy: exponential
```
We ship a helm values reference under `values-rate-limit.yaml` in private charts.

Matt (Eng-SRE): for k8s ingress, smoother option: use a local ingress-level queue (e.g., nginx `proxy_buffering on` + `proxy_busy_buffers_size`) or HAProxy with `tune.http.cooklen` to reduce upstream bursts. If you can add an Envoy local token bucket before the gateway it avoids large fan-ins.

AcmeInc - ops: is there a recommended probing/repro script? We want to reproduce safely.

Jules (Eng-Runtime): yes — small repro script we suggest: run 200 concurrent connections at steady ramp for 2 minutes then a 30s spike. Example (wrk-like):
```
wrk -t50 -c200 -d120s --latency http://<ingress>/predict
sleep 30
wrk -t50 -c800 -d30s --latency http://<ingress>/predict
```
Watch gateway metrics: `rw_gateway_rate_tokens`, `rw_gateway_burst_tokens`, and nginx `active connections`.

Matt (Eng-SRE): also capture tcpdump around the time to check SYN flood vs graceful keepalive reuse: `tcpdump -i any port 443 -w burst.pcap` then analyze in Wireshark for connection churn.

AcmeInc - ops: we'll run the repro during our maintenance window and report back. One extra thing — how do we avoid billing surprises if we bump burst?

Maria (Support): good question. For private deployments billing isn't usage-billed but we do have quota/commit mappings. If you bump burst you'll consume more capacity during spikes, so advise to monitor committed throughput and, if repeated, discuss reserved capacity. We can also set soft-limits and alerting to avoid surprise.

ops-bot: reminder — opened support ticket #SUP-2026-1187 and assigned to Eng-SRE for follow-up.

AcmeInc - ops: thanks. One last ask: any quick nginx snippet to add sliding window rate-limiting on ingress?

Aaditya (Eng-Platform): use the nginx `limit_req_zone` with `burst` and `nodelay` off to smooth: 
```
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=one:10m rate=50r/s;
server {
  location /predict {
    limit_req zone=one burst=100 nodelay;
    proxy_pass http://upstream_predict;
  }
}
```
Note: nodelay will allow bursts to pass immediately; omit nodelay for smoothing.

Matt (Eng-SRE): follow-up action items: 1) Acme run repro with metrics + pcap; 2) Acme bump gateway burst in staging 100->300 behind canary; 3) Aaditya to share helm values excerpt and safe defaults; 4) Jules to prepare runtime note on versions <1.8 and risk matrix.

Sara (Support): thanks everyone. Acme — reply here with repro results and we'll schedule a joint runbook session if needed. :thumbsup:

AcmeInc - ops: will do, thanks all.
